issues.failure_explanation: The cited classical results assume a fixed interaction kernel, while the model allows arbitrary measurable time-dependent controls $\varepsilon(t)$. For example, choosing $\varepsilon(t)=0$ or switching interactions off before consensus prevents finite-time clustering. Thus the claim is not supported by the cited results and is false for general admissible controls.

failure_location.quote: Classical results for opinion dynamics models~\cite{MotschTadmor2014} ensure that, under mild assumptions on $\phi$, the solution converges to a finite number of clusters in finite time.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim to fixed positive controls or add conditions on $\varepsilon$ ensuring persistent connectivity, or cite/prove a time-varying consensus result.
issues.overall_effect: The interpretation that the multi-agent dynamics automatically produces clusters for the model is unsupported.
issues.title: Finite-time clustering claim for time-dependent controls
issues.why_classification: Requires additional assumptions or a nontrivial argument; not a local typo.

issues.failure_explanation: In the expansion branch, the loop stops when the Armijo inequality fails. The algorithm then assigns $\sigma$ to this failed $\tau$, so the next step violates sufficient decrease. It should keep the last $\tau$ for which the inequality held.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Store the last successful $\tau$ in the expansion branch, or divide the final $\tau$ by $b$ once more before assigning $\sigma$.
issues.overall_effect: The DAL line search does not guarantee the stated Armijo decrease and may take non-descent steps.
issues.title: Two-way Armijo expansion uses failed step
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local logic correction to the line search and preserves the algorithm's intended behavior.

issues.failure_explanation: The line search evaluates the direction $-D$, but the update takes $+D$. With $D$ defined as $\partial_\varepsilon F\cdot\lambda$ for the stated adjoint system, the update is an ascent step, opposite to the checked descent direction. The algorithm as written does not perform the stated steepest descent.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the update to $\varepsilon^{(j+1)} \gets \Pi_E(\varepsilon^{(j)} - \sigma^{(j+1)} D^{(j)})$ or consistently flip the sign in all line-search tests.
issues.overall_effect: The DAL update direction is inconsistent with its line search, so the algorithm may increase the cost instead of decreasing it.
issues.title: Update uses opposite sign to line search
issues.why_classification: A local sign correction restores the intended descent update without changing the method.

issues.failure_explanation: The self term $j=i$ in the dynamics is $\phi(0)\cdot 0=0$, so its derivative with respect to $c_i$ is zero. The displayed sum includes $j=i$ and thus adds an incorrect term $-\phi(0)/N$. The sum should be over $j\neq i$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Exclude $j=i$ from the sum in the $k=i$ case.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete adjoint Jacobian used in the numerical DAL/ADMM schemes is incorrect by a constant diagonal term.
issues.title: Incorrect self-term in derivative of F_i with respect to c_i
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and routine, though it affects the adjoint computation.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where the compactly supported interaction kernel is given by the $C^2$ Wendland function

issues.failure_explanation: For $0\leq r<1/4$, $(4r-1)(1-r)^4$ is negative (e.g., $\varphi(0)=-1$). Hence it is not a nonnegative Wendland interaction kernel and makes nearby agents repel rather than align, contradicting the stated attraction/consensus model.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the kernel by a nonnegative compactly supported Wendland kernel, e.g. $(4r+1)(1-r)^4$ on $[0,1]$, and adjust derivative formulas accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The interaction model as written is not the intended attraction/consensus model; the numerical results and consensus interpretation based on this kernel are unreliable.
issues.title: Wendland kernel is negative near zero
issues.why_classification: A single local formula correction restores the intended nonnegative kernel and preserves the method.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: One should ensure that the compact set $E$ is large enough to allow both global interactions, i.e. $\phi(r_{ij}^\varepsilon)>0$ for any $i,j = 1,\ldots,N$, and no interactions at all, i.e. $\phi(r_{ij}^\varepsilon)=0$ for all $i,j = 1,\ldots,N$.

issues.failure_explanation: With $(x_i,y_i)\in[0,1]^2$, the maximum spatial squared distance is $2$ and the maximum colour squared difference is $1$, so the maximum possible $r$ is $\varepsilon_x+\varepsilon_c/2$. For $\varepsilon_x\geq 2$, this maximum is at least $2>1$, so $\phi=0$ for some pairs. Thus $E=[2,1100]^2$ does not allow global interactions for all $i,j$, contrary to the stated requirement.

failure_location.quote: In accordance with Remark~\ref{rmk:parameters}, we set $E = [2,1100]^2$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose a control set whose lower bound on $\varepsilon_x$ is small enough that $\varepsilon_x+\varepsilon_c/2<1$ for all admissible controls, or restate the numerical scope as local-interaction only.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical setup cannot realize the global-interaction regime claimed in the discussion of consensus and parameter choice.
issues.title: Chosen control set E forbids global interactions
issues.why_classification: A local parameter-range correction preserves the numerical method and the main claims.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: as in the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:existence1}, it is immediate to show coercivity in the primal variables, ensuring that the minimum is attained in a weakly compact set.

issues.failure_explanation: The term $|v|$ grows only linearly. After minimizing $v$, the reduced functional grows linearly in $\nabla u$, not quadratically, so sublevel sets are not bounded in $H^1$. The claimed coercivity in $H^1$ is false. For data whose ROF minimizer is not in $H^1$ (e.g., a step image), the primal problem has no minimizer in $H^1$ and hence no saddle point as stated.

failure_location.quote: There exists a saddle point for the functional $L : H^1(\Omega) \times L^2(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2) \times L^2(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2) \to \R$ defined in \eqref{eq:cost_tv_regular}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reformulate the primal space as $BV(\Omega)$ (or add strong enough regularity/coercivity assumptions) and prove attainment and strong duality there.
issues.overall_effect: The existence and strong-duality theorem for the regularized TV saddle-point formulation is invalid as stated, undermining the ADMM justification.
issues.title: No saddle point for L on H^1; coercivity proof fails
issues.why_classification: The theorem is false as stated and the proof's central coercivity step fails; repairing it requires changing the functional domain and proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we lose convexity in the control-to-state map $\varepsilon \mapsto c(\,\cdot\,,T; \varepsilon)$, so we can only expect convergence to a local minimum in the first variable.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:saddle_point concerns $L$ over a free $u\in H^1$, not over the image of the nonconvex control-to-state map $c(T;\varepsilon)$. Strong duality for the OCP does not follow and generally fails because minimization over $\varepsilon$ is nonconvex. Thus the claim that the theorem ensures no duality gap for the OCP is false.

failure_location.quote: This is the reason why Theorem \ref{thm:saddle_point} is fundamental: it ensures that there is no duality gap.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either prove a separate duality or convergence result for the nonconvex OCP, or remove the claim that Theorem thm:saddle_point eliminates the duality gap for the control problem.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical justification for applying ADMM to the nonconvex optimal control problem is invalid; the algorithm remains a heuristic without the claimed duality-gap guarantee.
issues.title: Saddle-point theorem does not imply no duality gap for nonconvex OCP
issues.why_classification: The misapplication affects the central theoretical justification of the ADMM approach and requires a new argument or a substantial weakening of the claim.
